clue.text: Country querying American lawyer's ability ?

parts.note: to have the ability is to be able, that is, you can
a DA, district attorney, is an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a US attorney is up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Querying' turns the pieces into a question: 'Can a DA?', which asks about an American lawyer's ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a nation of North America.

clue.text: Lodging here for Jonah and continental service in common US jail

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the jail word

parts.note: can is American slang for a prison
et is French, a continental language, for and
an ace is a winning serve in tennis

explanation.surface: Jonah's lodgings and European services compared to an American prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonah lodged inside a whale, so the definition names the creature, not a room. 'and continental' is French 'et'; a tennis serve that wins outright is an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales belong to the order Cetacea, the sea mammals, and Jonah was swallowed by one.

clue.text: Chemical can turn on speed

indicators.note: on means the second piece is placed after the first in this down clue
turn means the word for can is flipped end to end

parts.note: a tin is a can
rate is speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A chemical that can make someone high, like amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' tempts toward the drug, but it is just a rate; 'turn' flips the can word, and 'on' places the speed word after it in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Middleman supplies telephone receiver part

explanation.surface: An agent provides a spare phone component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' is the muscle wall dividing chest from belly, in the middle of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscular partition across the body's middle and the vibrating disc in an earpiece share this name.

clue.text: Such sopranos are back in the "public" eye

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: an optic is the measuring dispenser on a pub's spirit bottle, a pub-lic eye in the pun

indicators.note: back tells us to read the little word are from right to left

explanation.surface: Opera singers are once more in the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'public' signal the pun: pub-lic, belonging to a pub, where an optic is the dispenser that measures spirits; 'back' reverses ARE to make ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopranos of the opera stage sing in an operatic style.

clue.text: Not a case, one hopes, for Mrs Beeton to blow her top

definitions.text: Not a case, one hopes, for Mrs Beeton to blow her top

parts.words: Not a case, one hopes, for Mrs Beeton to blow her top
parts.note: a steam-sealed kitchen pan builds up force; the famous Victorian cookery writer hopes its lid does not fly off

explanation.surface: A situation in which the cook hopefully keeps her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton wrote Britain's best-known Victorian cookery book. 'Blow her top' means lose one's temper, but for this pan it is literally the lid flying off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed pan that cooks food fast under steam is a kitchen vessel full of stress that might explode.

clue.text: Splitter of sticks, say, for instance

definitions.text: Splitter of sticks, say, for instance

parts.words: Splitter of sticks, say, for instance
parts.note: one who rives wood splits it; and sticks said aloud is the Styx, a waterway of Hades

explanation.definitionFit: One who rives (splits) logs is a splitter, and the Styx is one of the flowing waterways of the underworld.

clue.text: Youngster detailed to go a-wooing

parts.note: in the nursery song 'a frog he would a-wooing go'; a young frog loses its tail before it grows up

explanation.surface: A young person told off to go courting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'assigned', but means de-tailed: the young creature loses its tail and becomes the frog of 'A Frog He Would A-Wooing Go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, which sheds its tail as it matures.

clue.text: "Be thou as — as ice, as pure as snow" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Be thou as — as ice, as pure as snow" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Be thou as — as ice, as pure as snow" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Hamlet tells Ophelia that even if she is pure, she will not escape slander; the gap wants a word for virtuous

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means sexually pure, virtuous, in Hamlet's line to Ophelia.

clue.text: Hit poem Richard composed of Middlesex ?

indicators.note: composed means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A successful poem Richard wrote about a London county.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex was an English county by London, but read as 'middle sex' it means between male and female.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermaphrodite has both male and female organs, so is of a sex in between.

clue.text: Paris summit conference ?

parts.note: in Paris a head is a tete, so a meeting of heads, face to face, is described in French

explanation.definitionFit: A private two-person meeting is literally head-to-head in French, the summit being the head.

clue.text: It's not what makes Mary look so bloody

definitions.text: It's not what makes Mary look so bloody

parts.words: It's not what makes Mary look so bloody
parts.note: a Bloody Mary cocktail gets its red colour from tomato juice, not from its colourless spirit

explanation.surface: Someone denies being the cause of Mary's gory appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'look' points to the colour: in a Bloody Mary the spirit is clear, so it is the tomato juice, not this, that makes the drink look bloody.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear Russian spirit is the alcoholic base of a Bloody Mary cocktail.

clue.text: Pitt sees the great Johnson eating his hat

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other and holds it inside

parts.note: Smollett called Samuel Johnson 'that great Cham of literature', cham being an old form of khan
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pitt watches Dr Johnson eat his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: William Pitt the Elder was made Earl of Chatham, so 'Pitt' is a name for the answer; CHATHAM is also a dockyard town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitt the Elder, the British prime minister, took the title Earl of Chatham.

clue.text: Garment as cut or designed for outdoors

indicators.note: designed means the letters of as cut or are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A coat cut and styled for wearing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges AS CUT OR into the answer; 'for outdoors' adds that the garment is worn over others.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcoat is a loose outer robe, once worn over a knight's armour.

clue.text: Girl might turn into a Mrs Swan

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading it from the end back to the start

parts.note: in myth Zeus came to Leda as a swan, so she is the swan's partner

explanation.surface: A girl may grow up to become a Mrs Swan by marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Leda, seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan, is the 'Mrs Swan'; 'might turn' reverses her name to ADEL and 'into a' sets A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adela is a woman's name.

clue.text: 1 Across's forty-ninth boundary

parts.note: Canada's border with the US follows a line of latitude, the forty-ninth

explanation.definitionFit: Lines of latitude are called parallels, and the 49th marks much of the Canada-US border.

clue.text: So to deal with a squeaker may be a bit cruel

definitions.text: So to deal with a squeaker

indicators.note: may be says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Dealing with a squealing animal this way could be a little unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: A squeaker is a squeaky hinge, not an animal; 'may be' rearranges A BIT CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiling a hinge or wheel stops it squeaking.

clue.text: Goddam dangerous creature if so treated

definitions.text: Goddam dangerous creature if so treated

parts.words: Goddam dangerous creature if so treated
parts.note: the letters of goddam read backwards spell a mad dog, a dangerous animal

explanation.definitionFit: Read backwards, the oath gives a rabid dog, so that is the treatment applied.

clue.text: Writing about eastern crime terribly entrancing

indicators.note: about means one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of crime are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A book about Eastern crime is horribly gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing' is a manuscript, MS; 'terribly' rearranges CRIME to MERIC, and 'about' puts MS around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mesmeric holds you spellbound, as if hypnotised.

clue.text: As high up as Richelieu's secretary?

definitions.text: As high up as Richelieu's secretary?

parts.words: As high up as Richelieu's secretary?
parts.note: Cardinal Richelieu's adviser, Father Joseph, was called the grey Eminence

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means distinguished, lofty; Richelieu's aide was nicknamed l'Eminence grise.

clue.text: Soundly founded instruction to one roasting a chicken

definitions.text: instruction to one roasting a chicken

indicators.note: soundly here means going by how a word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: founded on something means based on it

explanation.surface: Well-grounded advice for a cook roasting a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'firmly' but signals that BASED, said aloud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat over meat as it roasts; the cook is told to do it.

clue.text: Iron sort of cup

explanation.definitionFit: The rider's footrest hanging from a saddle is called an iron, and a parting drink taken on horseback is a cup named for it.

clue.text: Its power belongs to anyone who says so

definitions.text: Its power belongs to anyone who says so

parts.words: Its power belongs to anyone who says so
parts.note: anyone who can say a thing has the power of talking

explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of talking aloud is exercised by anyone saying something.

clue.text: Do such fast ladies distress Edward'?

parts.note: to distress is to pain
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Do loose women upset Edward?
explanation.walkthrough: Painted ladies, women in heavy make-up, were an old term for fast, immoral women.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted lady is a heavily made-up woman of loose morals.

clue.text: For a change, Doctor out of the House

indicators.note: for a change means these letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A doctor stepping out of Parliament for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' is the royal House of Tudor, not Parliament; 'For a change' rearranges DR and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII to Elizabeth I belonged to the royal dynasty of that name, England's ruling family 1485-1603.

clue.text: Mineral sort of oil, a source of wine

indicators.note: sort of means a variant form, so the letters of oil are mixed

parts.note: the grapevine is where wine comes from

explanation.surface: A sort of mineral oil from which wine comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges OIL to OLI; the vine is the plant wine comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Not all the men do the correct thing

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every man behaves properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE MEN Do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a text right by removing errors is to correct it.

clue.text: Tail-less bird includes "hairy man" in this book of words

indicators.note: includes means one piece goes inside the other
tail-less means the last letter of the bird is removed

parts.note: a thrush is a songbird
in Genesis Esau is 'a hairy man', unlike his brother Jacob

explanation.surface: A bird without its tail holds a shaggy man inside a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy man' is Genesis's description of Esau; 'Tail-less' drops the H from the end of the bird, giving THRUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing synonyms.

clue.text: Getting rabbits out on stage or field?

definitions.text: Getting rabbits out on stage or field?

parts.words: Getting rabbits out on stage or field?
parts.note: a magician pulls rabbits from a hat on stage; in cricket a rabbit is a poor batsman, and taking three wickets in a row is a celebrated feat

explanation.definitionFit: A hat trick is both a conjuring feat and, in cricket, three wickets taken with successive balls.

clue.text: How farmers cut their profits ?

parts.note: farmers harvest their crops with a blade, and crops are the gains of their year

explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a harvest, and also to gain a return.
